description: Allows removing a worktree, deleting/force-moving a branch, or recursively deleting files (git worktree remove/rm, git branch -d/-D/--delete/-f/-M/-C/-m/-c, git checkout -B, git switch -C, rm -r/-R/--recursive, git push --delete/--mirror/--prune/:ref, any git update-ref, rig worktree remove) ONLY when the work is landed and the tree is clean; denies anything that could destroy unmerged or uncommitted work. A cheap, deliberately loose prefilter (shell-style normalization of `$'..'`/`${IFS}`, quote/backslash stripping, flag prefixes and clusters, and shell expansion syntax in any command mentioning git/branch/push/worktree/update-ref or the rm word) decides whether a command is removal-shaped (STRICT) or merely contains expansion syntax (LOOSE, e.g. a heredoc commit); only then does the hook shell out to the PINNED rig (`--rig <absolute path>`, which `rig apply` substitutes for the /ABSOLUTE/PATH/TO/rig placeholder; never looked up on PATH) as `rig worktree guard --cwd <cwd>` (command on stdin), the single brain that parses the command and checks real git plus the forge PR state. The pinned rig must print `rig X.Y.Z` with X.Y.Z >= 0.64.0. Fails closed: a missing/non-absolute/non-executable pin, an unverifiable version, a nonzero exit, a timeout, or unparseable output denies; a rig older than 0.64.0 denies STRICT commands (upgrade rig) and allows LOOSE ones with a stderr warning. No bypass.
